correctness.rationale: Derived the first and mixed raw moments from Catalan root decomposition: T=x+T², C=2TC+x², S=2TS+x(T²)′, M=2TM+2CS+x(2TC)′+2x², with T=(1-sqrt(1-4x))/2. The finite coefficient identities imply Cov(C_n,S_n)=n/(2n-3)*(n-1-n q_n/4), q_n=4^(n-1)/binom(2n-2,n-1). Independent enumeration of every plane binary tree for n2..8 gave covariance 0,0,-4/25,-20/49,-46/63,-406/363,-8744/5577, matching the formula; checked cherry variance from marker second derivative. Exact adjacent ratio q_(n+1)/q_n=2n/(2n-1) exceeds a_(n+1)/a_n=n²/(n²-1), a_n=4(n-1)/n, yielding negative covariance for all n≥4, not a finite extrapolation. Established uniform-model Sackin variance asymptotic (10/3-pi)n³ is explicitly cited external input; Catalan central binomial asymptotic then gives covariance ~-sqrt(pi)n^(3/2)/8 and sqrt(n) Corr→-sqrt(pi)/(2sqrt(10/3-pi)). Correlation undefined n2,3 because Var C_n=0.

value.rationale: Cherry count is a standard local shape index and Sackin depth a standard global imbalance index, making their covariance and sharp decorrelation rate a natural quantitative test of redundant information in a phylogenetic null model. An exact sign boundary at n4 and the explicit asymptotic constant are meaningful beyond separately known marginal moments.
